description: Language-neutral contract definition strategy. Contracts must not depend on TypeScript, because the same contract must one day be honoured by JS, Rust, a WASM adapter and an external API. This file fixes the strategy and the minimal type vocabulary. It deliberately does NOT build a code generator — that is a later phase, and a generator written before there are real contracts to generate is a liability.

decision.chosen: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) subset, stored as data next to each contract

alternatives.option: TypeScript types as the source of truth
alternatives.rejectedBecause: not language-neutral: Rust and WASM cannot consume it, and it would make TS the architecture rather than an implementation detail
imposes a serialization model on in-process direct calls, which the foundation forbids; also adds a compiler to the toolchain

alternatives.option: OpenAPI as the source of truth
alternatives.rejectedBecause: HTTP-shaped by construction, which would violate transport neutrality
maximum cost, no ecosystem, and nothing here needs it

decision.because: A JSON Schema subset is data, has generators for every target language when we eventually need them, validates at runtime without a build step, and imposes nothing on direct in-process calls.

semantic.json: arbitrary JSON value — use sparingly; it defeats cross-language checking
semantic.binaryRef: reference to binary data held by the binary-data contract, never inline bytes

typeVocabulary.rule: Prefer the narrowest type. `json` is an escape hatch that a future Rust binding cannot type — every use is technical debt and should be justified in the contract.

contractDefinition.location: each public contract MAY ship `contract.schema.json` next to its `contract/index.mjs`

<operationName>.errors: error codes this operation may raise, from the LEGO error contract
<operationName>.semantics: idempotency, determinism, atomicity, concurrency, cancellable, backpressure

contractDefinition.adoptionRule: OPTIONAL in P2.8-B and MANDATORY for any contract that gains a second binding (worker, remote, Rust or WASM). A purely in-process JS contract does not pay the cost until it has to.

in-process-js.note: typed objects passed by reference; validating on every direct call would be a pointless tax

remote-api.validation: on entry, always — it is a trust boundary

generationPolicy.now: none. Schemas are hand-written data where they exist.
generationPolicy.later: a small generator may emit JS validators, Rust structs and an OpenAPI document from the same schema. It must remain optional — the schema is the source of truth, generated code is a convenience.
generationPolicy.rule: No generated artifact may ever become the source of truth.
